import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Nagata's conjecture on curves

Nagata's conjecture governs the minimal degree required for a plane algebraic curve to pass
through a collection of very general points with prescribed multiplicities.

**Nagata's conjecture.** Suppose $p_1, \ldots, p_r$ are very general points in $\mathbb{P}^2$
and that $m_1, \ldots, m_r$ are given positive integers. Then for $r > 9$ any curve $C$ in
$\mathbb{P}^2$ that passes through each of the points $p_i$ with multiplicity $m_i$ must
satisfy
$$\deg C > \frac{1}{\sqrt{r}} \sum_{i=1}^r m_i.$$

The condition $r > 9$ is necessary. The only case known to hold is when $r$ is a perfect
square, which was proved by Nagata.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagata%27s_conjecture_on_curves)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics#Algebraic_geometry)
- M. Nagata, *On the 14-th problem of Hilbert*, Amer. J. Math. 81 (1959), 766–772.
- B. Harbourne, *On Nagata's conjecture*, J. Algebra 236 (2001), 692–702,
  [arXiv:math/9909093](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9909093).
-/

namespace NagatasConjectureOnCurves

open MvPolynomial
open scoped LinearAlgebra.Projectivization

variable {k : Type*} [Field k]

/-- The homogeneous ideal $I(p) \subseteq k[X_0, X_1, X_2]$ of a point $p \in \mathbb{P}^2$:
the polynomials vanishing on the line of $k^3$ that represents $p$.
For `k` infinite it is the prime ideal generated by the linear forms vanishing at $p$. -/
def pointIdeal (p : ℙ k (Fin 3 → k)) : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin 3) k) :=
  vanishingIdeal k (p.submodule : Set (Fin 3 → k))

/-- A plane curve $C = \{F = 0\}$, given by a homogeneous polynomial $F \in k[X_0, X_1, X_2]$,
has multiplicity at least $m$ at the point $p \in \mathbb{P}^2$ if $F \in I(p)^m$, where $I(p)$
is the homogeneous ideal of $p$. Concretely, in coordinates with $p = [0 : 0 : 1]$, this says
that every monomial of $F$ has degree at least $m$ in $X_0, X_1$, i.e. that the affine equation
$F(x, y, 1)$ vanishes to order at least $m$ at the origin. -/
def HasMultiplicityAtLeast (F : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) k) (p : ℙ k (Fin 3 → k)) (m : ℕ) : Prop :=
  F ∈ pointIdeal p ^ m

/-- A subset $S$ of $(\mathbb{P}^2)^r$ is Zariski closed if there is an ideal $I$ of polynomials
in the $3r$ homogeneous coordinates such that $S$ consists of exactly those
$p = (p_1, \ldots, p_r)$ for which every tuple $(v_1, \ldots, v_r)$ with $v_i$ on the line
representing $p_i$ is a common zero of $I$. (For a multihomogeneous ideal $I$ this is the usual
zero locus of $I$; for `k` infinite, every ideal defines the same set as the ideal generated by the
multihomogeneous components of its elements.) -/
def IsZariskiClosed {r : ℕ} (S : Set (Fin r → ℙ k (Fin 3 → k))) : Prop :=
  ∃ I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin r × Fin 3) k),
    S = {p | ∀ v : Fin r × Fin 3 → k, (∀ i, (fun j ↦ v (i, j)) ∈ (p i).submodule) →
      v ∈ zeroLocus k I}

/-- A property `Q` of $r$-tuples of points of $\mathbb{P}^2$ holds for *very general* points if
it holds for every tuple outside a countable union of proper Zariski closed subsets
of $(\mathbb{P}^2)^r$. -/
def VeryGeneral {r : ℕ} (Q : (Fin r → ℙ k (Fin 3 → k)) → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ Z : ℕ → Set (Fin r → ℙ k (Fin 3 → k)),
    (∀ n, IsZariskiClosed (Z n) ∧ Z n ≠ Set.univ) ∧ ∀ p, p ∉ ⋃ n, Z n → Q p

/-- **Nagata's conjecture on curves.** Let $r > 9$. Suppose $p_1, \ldots, p_r$ are very general
points in $\mathbb{P}^2$ (over $\mathbb{C}$) and $m_1, \ldots, m_r$ are positive integers. Then
any plane curve $C$ (given by a nonzero homogeneous polynomial $F$ of degree $d$, not
necessarily reduced or irreducible) passing through each $p_i$ with multiplicity at least
$m_i$ satisfies
$$\deg C > \frac{1}{\sqrt{r}} \sum_{i=1}^r m_i.$$
The hypothesis $r > 9$ is necessary: for $r = 9$ a cubic through nine very general points
has $\deg C = 3 = \frac{1}{\sqrt 9} \sum_{i=1}^9 1$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 14]
theorem nagatas_conjecture_on_curves (r : ℕ) (hr : 9 < r) :
    VeryGeneral fun p : Fin r → ℙ ℂ (Fin 3 → ℂ) ↦
      ∀ m : Fin r → ℕ, (∀ i, 0 < m i) →
        ∀ (d : ℕ) (F : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℂ), F ≠ 0 → F.IsHomogeneous d →
          (∀ i, HasMultiplicityAtLeast F (p i) (m i)) →
            (∑ i, (m i : ℝ)) / √r < d := by
  sorry

/-- **Nagata's conjecture on curves**, existential form. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed
field of characteristic zero, $r > 9$, $m_1, \ldots, m_r$ positive integers and $d$ a
natural number with $d \sqrt{r} \le \sum_{i=1}^r m_i$. Then there are $r$ distinct points
$p_1, \ldots, p_r \in \mathbb{P}^2$ such that no plane curve of degree $d$ passes through each
$p_i$ with multiplicity at least $m_i$.

For fixed $d$ and $m_i$, the set of $r$-tuples of points admitting such a curve is Zariski
closed, so this is equivalent to `nagatas_conjecture_on_curves`; this is the form in which
Harbourne states the conjecture ($d(m, n) > m \sqrt{n}$ for $n \ge 10$). -/
@[category research open, AMS 14]
theorem nagatas_conjecture_on_curves.variants.exists_points {k : Type*} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    [CharZero k] (r : ℕ) (hr : 9 < r) (m : Fin r → ℕ) (hm : ∀ i, 0 < m i) (d : ℕ)
    (hd : (d : ℝ) * √r ≤ ∑ i, (m i : ℝ)) :
    ∃ p : Fin r → ℙ k (Fin 3 → k), Function.Injective p ∧
      ∀ F : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) k, F ≠ 0 → F.IsHomogeneous d →
        ¬ ∀ i, HasMultiplicityAtLeast F (p i) (m i) := by
  sorry

section Tests

/-- Every curve has multiplicity at least `0` at every point. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem hasMultiplicityAtLeast_zero (F : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) k) (p : ℙ k (Fin 3 → k)) :
    HasMultiplicityAtLeast F p 0 := by
  simp [HasMultiplicityAtLeast]

/-- Multiplicity at least `n` implies multiplicity at least `m` for `m ≤ n`. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem HasMultiplicityAtLeast.mono {F : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) k} {p : ℙ k (Fin 3 → k)}
    {m n : ℕ} (hmn : m ≤ n) (h : HasMultiplicityAtLeast F p n) : HasMultiplicityAtLeast F p m :=
  Ideal.pow_le_pow_right hmn h

/-- The pair of lines `X₀ X₁ = 0` has a double point at `[0 : 0 : 1]`. -/
@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem hasMultiplicityAtLeast_X_mul_X :
    HasMultiplicityAtLeast (X 0 * X 1 : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) k)
      (Projectivization.mk k ![0, 0, 1] (by simp)) 2 := by
  have h : ∀ i, i ≠ 2 → (X i : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) k) ∈
      pointIdeal (Projectivization.mk k ![0, 0, 1] (by simp)) := by
    intro i hi
    rw [pointIdeal, mem_vanishingIdeal_iff]
    intro x hx
    rw [SetLike.mem_coe, Projectivization.submodule_mk, Submodule.mem_span_singleton] at hx
    obtain ⟨a, rfl⟩ := hx
    fin_cases i <;> simp_all
  rw [HasMultiplicityAtLeast, pow_two]
  exact Ideal.mul_mem_mul (h 0 (by decide)) (h 1 (by decide))

/-- The empty set is Zariski closed. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem isZariskiClosed_empty {r : ℕ} : IsZariskiClosed (∅ : Set (Fin r → ℙ k (Fin 3 → k))) := by
  refine ⟨⊤, ?_⟩
  ext p
  simp only [Set.mem_empty_iff_false, Set.mem_setOf_eq, zeroLocus_top, false_iff, not_forall]
  exact ⟨0, fun i ↦ Submodule.zero_mem _, by simp⟩

/-- The whole space is Zariski closed. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem isZariskiClosed_univ {r : ℕ} :
    IsZariskiClosed (Set.univ : Set (Fin r → ℙ k (Fin 3 → k))) := by
  refine ⟨⊥, ?_⟩
  ext p
  simp

/-- A property that holds everywhere holds for very general points. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem VeryGeneral.of_forall {r : ℕ} {Q : (Fin r → ℙ k (Fin 3 → k)) → Prop} (h : ∀ p, Q p) :
    VeryGeneral Q :=
  ⟨fun _ ↦ ∅, fun _ ↦ ⟨isZariskiClosed_empty, Set.empty_ne_univ⟩, fun p _ ↦ h p⟩

end Tests

end NagatasConjectureOnCurves

'Passes through p_i with multiplicity m_i' is read as 'multiplicity at least m_i' (equivalent formulation, per the notes).

'Very general' is made explicit: `VeryGeneral Q` := ∃ Z : ℕ → Set ((ℙ²)^r), each Z n Zariski closed and ≠ univ, and Q holds off ⋃ Z n. `IsZariskiClosed S` := ∃ ideal I ⊆ k[3r variables] with S = {p | every tuple of vectors lying on the lines representing the p_i is in `MvPolynomial.zeroLocus k I`}. Quantifier order: the countable family of closed sets depends only on r (placed before m, d, F), matching the literal reading 'suppose p_i very general and m_i given'; since the m range over a countable set this is equivalent to letting it depend on m.
Inequality written as (∑ (m i : ℝ)) / √r < d, matching deg C > (1/√r) ∑ m_i literally; strict; r > 9 so √r > 0 and division is harmless.

Added a variant `nagatas_conjecture_on_curves.variants.exists_points` over an arbitrary algebraically closed field of characteristic zero in Harbourne's existential form: for r > 9, positive m_i and d with d√r ≤ ∑ m_i there exist r distinct points admitting no degree-d curve with multiplicity ≥ m_i at each point. /--
**Nagata's conjecture on curves.** Let $r>9$, and let $m_1,\ldots,m_r$ be positive
integers. For very general points $p_1,\ldots,p_r$ of the complex projective plane, every
nonzero plane curve having multiplicity at least $m_i$ at $p_i$ has degree $d$ satisfying
$d\sqrt r>\sum_i m_i$.

This is stated in the equivalent semicontinuity form: whenever
$d\sqrt r\leq\sum_i m_i$, there is a configuration of $r$ distinct points admitting no such
curve of degree $d$. The points are chosen in an affine chart. A polynomial has multiplicity
at least $m_i$ at $(a_i,b_i)$ exactly when it belongs to the $m_i$-th power of the maximal
ideal $(X-a_i,Y-b_i)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 14]
theorem nagatas_conjecture_on_curves :
    ∀ (r : ℕ) (m : Fin r → ℕ) (d : ℕ),
      9 < r →
      (∀ i, 0 < m i) →
      (d : ℝ) * Real.sqrt r ≤ ∑ i, (m i : ℝ) →
      ∃ p : Fin r → (Fin 2 → ℂ),
        Function.Injective p ∧
          ¬ ∃ f : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℂ,
            f ≠ 0 ∧
              f.totalDegree ≤ d ∧
                ∀ i,
                  f ∈ (Ideal.span
                    ({MvPolynomial.X 0 - MvPolynomial.C (p i 0),
                      MvPolynomial.X 1 - MvPolynomial.C (p i 1)} :
                      Set (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℂ))) ^ m i := by
  sorry

end NagatasConjectureOnCurves

This avoids requiring a missing library notion of a countable-union complement of proper Zariski-closed subsets.
Specialized the algebraically closed uncountable base field to ℂ.

Represented the chosen projective points in the standard affine chart as elements of `Fin 2 → ℂ`, with `Function.Injective p` imposing distinctness. Dehomogenization identifies homogeneous projective polynomials of degree d with affine polynomials of total degree at most d; conversely, homogenization to degree d preserves multiplicities at these affine points.
Expressed multiplicity at least m at `(a,b)` by membership in `(X-a, Y-b)^m`, the m-th power of the point's maximal ideal in the bivariate polynomial ring.
Stated the forbidden range as `d * sqrt r ≤ ∑ m_i`, so nonexistence there is exactly equivalent to the conjecture's strict inequality `deg C * sqrt r > ∑ m_i`.
Allowed every nonzero polynomial, with no reducedness or irreducibility hypothesis, as required.

namespace NagatasConjectureOnCurves

open MvPolynomial
open scoped LinearAlgebra.Projectivization

/-- The complex projective plane $\mathbb{P}^2$, as the projectivization of $\mathbb{C}^3$. -/
local notation "ℙ²" => ℙ ℂ (Fin 3 → ℂ)

/-- A polynomial `F` in the homogeneous coordinates $X_0, X_1, X_2$ of $\mathbb{P}^2$ has
multiplicity at least `m` at the point `p` if `F` lies in the `m`-th power of the maximal ideal
of every vector `v ∈ ℂ³` of homogeneous coordinates of `p`. That is, all Taylor coefficients of
`F` at `v` of total degree less than `m` vanish.

For a nonzero homogeneous `F` this is exactly the condition that the plane curve $\{F = 0\}$
passes through `p` with multiplicity at least `m` (the multiplicity of the affine cone at `v`
equals the multiplicity of the curve at `p`, and it is independent of the choice of `v`). -/
def HasMultiplicityAtLeast (F : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℂ) (m : ℕ) (p : ℙ²) : Prop :=
  ∀ (v : Fin 3 → ℂ) (hv : v ≠ 0), Projectivization.mk ℂ v hv = p →
    F ∈ (vanishingIdeal ℂ {v}) ^ m

/-- A subset `Z` of $(\mathbb{P}^2)^r$ is Zariski closed if it is the common zero set of a family
`S` of polynomials in the `3r` homogeneous coordinates, where a point `p` counts as a zero of
`F ∈ S` if `F` vanishes at every choice `v` of homogeneous coordinates of `p`.

Since `ℂ` is infinite, `F` vanishes at every choice of homogeneous coordinates of `p` if and
only if each multihomogeneous component of `F` does, so this agrees with the usual definition
via multihomogeneous polynomials. -/
def IsZariskiClosed {r : ℕ} (Z : Set (Fin r → ℙ²)) : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Set (MvPolynomial (Fin r × Fin 3) ℂ),
    Z = {p | ∀ F ∈ S, ∀ v : Fin r → Fin 3 → ℂ,
      (∀ i, ∃ hv : v i ≠ 0, Projectivization.mk ℂ (v i) hv = p i) →
        eval (fun ij => v ij.1 ij.2) F = 0}

/--
**Nagata's conjecture on curves.** Let $r > 9$ and let $m_1, \dots, m_r$ be positive integers.
If $p_1, \dots, p_r \in \mathbb{P}^2$ are very general points (that is, they lie outside a
countable union of proper Zariski closed subsets of $(\mathbb{P}^2)^r$, which may depend on $r$
and on $m_1, \dots, m_r$), then any plane curve $C$ of degree $d$ passing through each $p_i$
with multiplicity at least $m_i$ satisfies
$$d \sqrt{r} > \sum_{i=1}^r m_i.$$

Here a plane curve of degree $d$ is given by a nonzero homogeneous polynomial $F$ of degree $d$
in three variables over $\mathbb{C}$; it need not be reduced or irreducible.
The hypothesis $r > 9$ is necessary: for $r = 9$ a cubic through $9$ general points with
multiplicity $1$ gives $d\sqrt{r} = 9 = \sum m_i$.

The conjecture is known only when $r$ is a perfect square (Nagata, 1959).

* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagata%27s_conjecture_on_curves)

Nagata's conjecture on curves governs the minimal degree required for a plane algebraic curve to
pass through a collection of very general points with prescribed multiplicities:

**Nagata's conjecture.** Suppose $p_1, \dots, p_r$ are very general points in $\mathbb{P}^2$ and
$m_1, \dots, m_r$ are given positive integers. Then for $r > 9$ any curve $C$ in $\mathbb{P}^2$
that passes through each of the points $p_i$ with multiplicity $m_i$ must satisfy
$$\deg C > \frac{1}{\sqrt r} \sum_{i=1}^r m_i.$$

The condition $r > 9$ is necessary (for $r = 9$ a cubic through nine points has
$\deg C = 3 = \frac{1}{\sqrt 9} \sum m_i$). The only known case is when $r$ is a perfect square,
which was proved by Nagata [Nag59].

## Formalisation choices

* We work over $\mathbb{C}$, and $\mathbb{P}^2$ is the projectivization `ℙ ℂ (Fin 3 → ℂ)` of
  $\mathbb{C}^3$.
* A plane curve of degree $d$ is a nonzero homogeneous polynomial $F$ of degree $d$ in the
  homogeneous coordinates $X_0, X_1, X_2$; it need not be reduced or irreducible.
* The curve $F = 0$ passes through $p$ with multiplicity (at least) $m$ iff $F$ lies in the $m$-th
  power of the homogeneous ideal `pointIdeal p` of $p$, which is generated by the linear forms
  vanishing at $p$. (In affine coordinates centred at $p$ this says that $F$ has no terms of
  degree $< m$, the usual definition of the multiplicity of a curve at a point.)
* "Very general" has its standard meaning: the property holds for all $r$-tuples of points
  outside a countable union of proper Zariski closed subsets of $(\mathbb{P}^2)^r$. Since
  $\mathbb{C}$ is uncountable, such tuples exist.
-/

# Nagata's conjecture on curves

Nagata's conjecture on curves governs the minimal degree required for a plane algebraic curve
to pass through a collection of very general points with prescribed multiplicities.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Nagata's conjecture on curves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagata%27s_conjecture_on_curves)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Nag59] M. Nagata, *On the 14-th problem of Hilbert*, Amer. J. Math. 81 (1959), 766–772.

- [Har01] B. Harbourne, *On Nagata's conjecture*, J. Algebra 236 (2001), 692–702.

open MvPolynomial
open scoped LinearAlgebra.Projectivization

namespace NagatasConjectureOnCurves

variable {k : Type*} [Field k]

/-- The ideal of a point `p` of the projective plane `ℙ²(k) = ℙ k (Fin 3 → k)`: the ideal of
polynomials in `k[X₀, X₁, X₂]` vanishing on the line in `k³` represented by `p`.
Over an infinite field, this is the homogeneous ideal of `p`, generated by the linear forms
vanishing at `p`. -/
def pointIdeal (p : ℙ k (Fin 3 → k)) : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin 3) k) :=
  vanishingIdeal k (p.submodule : Set (Fin 3 → k))

/-- A polynomial `F ∈ k[X₀, X₁, X₂]` *has multiplicity at least `m`* at a point
`p ∈ ℙ²(k)` if `F` lies in the `m`-th power of the ideal of `p`. For a nonzero form `F`, this
says that the plane curve `F = 0` passes through `p` with multiplicity at least `m`, i.e.
vanishes to order at least `m` at `p`. -/
def HasMultiplicityAtLeast (F : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) k) (p : ℙ k (Fin 3 → k)) (m : ℕ) :
    Prop :=
  F ∈ pointIdeal p ^ m

/-- The ideal of a point is a proper ideal. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem pointIdeal_ne_top (p : ℙ k (Fin 3 → k)) : pointIdeal p ≠ ⊤ := by
  intro h
  have h1 := (Ideal.eq_top_iff_one _).1 h
  simpa [pointIdeal, mem_vanishingIdeal_iff] using h1 0 (Submodule.zero_mem _)

/-- Every polynomial has multiplicity at least `0` at every point. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem hasMultiplicityAtLeast_zero (F : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) k) (p : ℙ k (Fin 3 → k)) :
    HasMultiplicityAtLeast F p 0 := by
  simp [HasMultiplicityAtLeast]

/-- Multiplicity at least `1` at `p` means vanishing at `p`, i.e. on the line represented by `p`. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem hasMultiplicityAtLeast_one_iff (F : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) k) (p : ℙ k (Fin 3 → k)) :
    HasMultiplicityAtLeast F p 1 ↔ ∀ v ∈ p.submodule, aeval v F = 0 := by
  simp [HasMultiplicityAtLeast, pointIdeal, mem_vanishingIdeal_iff]

/-- Multiplicity at least `m` implies multiplicity at least `n` whenever `n ≤ m`. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem HasMultiplicityAtLeast.mono {F : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) k} {p : ℙ k (Fin 3 → k)}
    {m n : ℕ} (h : HasMultiplicityAtLeast F p m) (hnm : n ≤ m) :
    HasMultiplicityAtLeast F p n :=
  Ideal.pow_le_pow_right hnm h

/-- The conic `X₁ X₂ = 0` (a pair of lines) has a double point at `[1 : 0 : 0]`. -/
@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem hasMultiplicityAtLeast_X_mul_X :
    HasMultiplicityAtLeast (X 1 * X 2 : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) k)
      (Projectivization.mk k (Pi.single 0 1) (by simp)) 2 := by
  have h : ∀ i : Fin 3, i ≠ 0 → (X i : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) k) ∈
      pointIdeal (Projectivization.mk k (Pi.single 0 1) (by simp)) := by
    intro i hi
    simp only [pointIdeal, mem_vanishingIdeal_iff, SetLike.mem_coe, Projectivization.submodule_mk,
      Submodule.mem_span_singleton]
    rintro v ⟨c, rfl⟩
    simp [hi]
  rw [HasMultiplicityAtLeast, pow_two]
  exact Ideal.mul_mem_mul (h 1 (by decide)) (h 2 (by decide))

/-- **Nagata's conjecture on curves.** Let `k` be an algebraically closed field. Suppose
$p_1, \dots, p_r$ are very general points in $\mathbb{P}^2$ and $m_1, \dots, m_r$ are positive

least $m_i$ satisfies
$$\deg C > \frac{1}{\sqrt r} \sum_{i=1}^r m_i.$$

$F \in k[X_0, X_1, X_2]$ of degree $d$ (not necessarily reduced or irreducible), and $C$ passes
through $p_i$ with multiplicity at least $m_i$ when $F \in I(p_i)^{m_i}$, where $I(p_i)$ is the
homogeneous ideal of the point $p_i$.

very general points is equivalent to the same statement for general points, i.e. to the existence
of one configuration of $r$ distinct points for which every curve with the prescribed
multiplicities satisfies the inequality; this is the form stated here. As in [Har01], the ground
field is an arbitrary algebraically closed field.

inequality. -/

    (m : Fin r → ℕ) (hm : ∀ i, 0 < m i) :
    ∃ p : Fin r → ℙ k (Fin 3 → k), Function.Injective p ∧
      ∀ (d : ℕ) (F : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) k), F ≠ 0 → F.IsHomogeneous d →
        (∀ i, HasMultiplicityAtLeast F (p i) (m i)) →
        ∑ i, (m i : ℝ) < d * √r := by
  sorry

(with $s \ge 4$, i.e. $r > 9$). Here it is stated, as in [Har01], for a uniform multiplicity $m$:
for general points $p_1, \dots, p_{s^2}$, any curve of degree $d$ passing through each $p_i$

    (s : ℕ) (hs : 4 ≤ s) (m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) :

      ∀ (d : ℕ) (F : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) k), F ≠ 0 → F.IsHomogeneous d →
        (∀ i, HasMultiplicityAtLeast F (p i) m) →
        m * s < d := by
  sorry

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Nagata's conjecture on curves

Nagata's conjecture gives a lower bound for the degree of a plane algebraic curve through very
general points with prescribed multiplicities.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Nagata's conjecture on curves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagata%27s_conjecture_on_curves)
-/

open scoped LinearAlgebra.Projectivization

namespace NagatasConjectureOnCurves

/--
Nagata's conjecture: for `r > 9` and positive integers $m_1,\ldots,m_r$, every plane
curve $C$ through very general points $p_1,\ldots,p_r \in \mathbb{P}^2_{\mathbb C}$ with
multiplicity at least $m_i$ at $p_i$ satisfies
$\deg(C)\sqrt r > \sum_i m_i$.

Equivalently, for every degree $d$ with $d\sqrt r \leq \sum_i m_i$, there is a configuration
of `r` distinct projective points for which no such degree-$d$ curve exists. For a projective
point `p`, the kernel of the map $X_j \mapsto p_jT$ is its homogeneous ideal; membership in
its $m_i$-th power expresses multiplicity at least $m_i$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 14]
theorem nagatas_conjecture_on_curves :
    ∀ (r : ℕ) (m : Fin r → ℕ) (d : ℕ),
      9 < r →
      (∀ i, 0 < m i) →
      (d : ℝ) * Real.sqrt r ≤ ∑ i, (m i : ℝ) →
      ∃ p : Fin r → ℙ ℂ (Fin 3 → ℂ),
        Function.Injective p ∧
          ¬ ∃ f : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℂ,
            f ≠ 0 ∧ f.IsHomogeneous d ∧
              ∀ i,
                f ∈ (RingHom.ker
                  (MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom Polynomial.C fun j =>
                    Polynomial.C ((p i).rep j) * Polynomial.X)) ^ m i := by
  sorry

end NagatasConjectureOnCurves
modeling_decisions: Specialized the algebraically closed ground field to ℂ, as explicitly permitted by the decomposition notes and ensuring the intended very-general-point setting.

Used the semicontinuity-equivalent existential formulation specified in the decomposition notes: for every forbidden degree d, there exists a distinct configuration admitting no curve of that degree with the prescribed multiplicities.

Represented the homogeneous ideal of a projective point p as the kernel of the ring homomorphism sending each coordinate X_j to p_j T in ℂ[T]. For a homogeneous polynomial, membership in the m-th power of this ideal is the standard condition that its projective multiplicity at p is at least m.
Represented a plane curve by an arbitrary nonzero homogeneous polynomial of degree d; no reducedness or irreducibility condition is imposed.
